mainTopic: Shabbat 113a: Temporary knots on a bucket, moving a weaver's loom parts, folding clothes on שבת, and honoring שבת through dress, walking and speech.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point about temporary knots. רב יוסף then rules like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and אביי insists on knowing whether חכמים disagree, because Torah is not a song to repeat without understanding. A new משנה allows tying a bucket with a belt but not a rope, while רבי יהודה permits the rope. The גמרא explains that the rope is a weaver's rope, and it settles an apparent contradiction from a ברייתא: רבנן decree only where confusion is likely, and רבי יהודה holds a bow is itself a knot. Next, the גמרא discusses which loom parts may be moved on שבת. Weavers' tools and beams may be moved according to שמואל, but the posts may not, because a person might fill in the holes in his house; רבי יהודה בר ליואי forbids moving the heavy beams. A second משנה deals with folding clothes, making beds, and burning sacrificial fats when שבת and יום הכיפורים fall next to each other. The גמרא limits folding to one person folding a new, white garment when he has nothing else to wear. It then teaches how to honor שבת with clothing, walking and speech, based on a פסוק in ישעיה, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even when one knot is undone, both still count as temporary
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of an answer from the previous discussion. You might have thought that because one of the two knots gets undone, the other counts as a permanent knot. The teaching comes to tell us that is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: [You might have thought that since] one of them he voids, [the other is permanent]. It teaches us [that both are temporary and allowed].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began on the previous amud. It explains why the earlier teaching about knots on an animal needed to be stated at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא asked why something obvious needed saying. The answer: since the person only undoes one knot to free the animal, we might think the other knot stays forever and counts as permanent. The phrase קא משמע לן tells us the teaching rejects that idea, so both knots are treated as temporary.

keyTerms.meaning: He actually voids it (he undoes or abandons it)
It teaches us (introduces the new point a teaching comes to make)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'you might have thought' (מהו דתימא) come on the previous amud, so read this line as the end of that thought.

phrases.english: [since] one of them he voids,
phrases.notes: This continues the 'you might have thought' (מהו דתימא) from the line before.

phrases.english: it teaches us [that both are temporary knots].
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא wraps up a מהו דתימא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: explaining why a seemingly obvious teaching was needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since one knot is undone, the other might be considered permanent
steps.terutzMaskana: Both knots are considered temporary and permitted

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports, in the name of רב יהודה and שמואל, that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב on tying an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said that רב יהודה said that שמואל said: The הלכה is like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a practical ruling on the earlier dispute. The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple ruling passed down through a chain of teachers. It settles the practical question. The next steps question what the ruling implies about whether there was a real dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha follows (the practical ruling is like) ...

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the earlier dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The practical halacha follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: אביי asks whether a ruling implies a disagreement
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: if you say 'the הלכה is like him,' that implies others disagree. Do they really?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: 'The הלכה [is like him]' implies that they disagree [does it?].
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions רב יוסף about the wording of the ruling. Saying 'the halacha is like X' normally means someone argues with X.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we only say 'the הלכה is like so-and-so' when there is a disagreement to decide. אביי wants to know if חכמים truly argue with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, or if everyone agrees with him.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
'The halacha [is like him]' — implies that they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the ruling in Step 2 implies
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חכמים actually disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: רב יוסף asks what practical difference it makes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers with a question: what difference does it make to you? Either way, the halacha is like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What difference does it make to you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on אביי's question. Since the practical ruling is the same either way, why bother asking?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's point is that the outcome does not change. Whether or not חכמים disagree, we follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He dismisses the question as having no practical result.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to you? (what is the practical result?)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי נָפְקָא לָךְ מִינַּהּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: What difference does it make to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the question in Step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the need to ask the question at all
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question has no practical halachic result

steps.title: Torah is not a song to repeat without understanding
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a folk saying: should learning be like a song you sing without understanding? We must understand the sugya, even when nothing practical depends on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Learn the learning, and let it be a song'?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his question. Torah learning means understanding, not just memorizing the bottom line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי rejects the idea that only practical results matter. Knowing whether a dispute exists is part of truly understanding the תורה, even if the ruling stays the same. This closes the exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn the learning (just memorize the tradition)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי teaches a key principle of learning: we analyze a sugya to understand it, not only to find a practical ruling. Torah is not a song to repeat without thinking.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is often quoted as the source for studying Torah in depth, even where there is no practical difference (נפקא מינה).

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גְּמָרָא גְּמוֹר זְמוֹרְתָּא תְּהֵא?!
phrases.english: He said to him: Learn the learning, and let it be a song?!
phrases.notes: A popular saying: learning has to be understood, not just sung.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's pushback in Step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We must understand the תורה even without a practical difference

steps.title: משנה: tying a bucket with a belt or a rope
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may tie a bucket with a belt (פסקיא) on שבת but not with a rope (חבל). רבי יהודה permits even the rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may tie a bucket with a belt, but not with a rope. רבי יהודה permits.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses which materials one may use to tie a bucket on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A belt will surely be taken off later, so its knot is temporary and allowed. A rope might be left tied, so the first opinion forbids it. רבי יהודה disagrees and permits the rope too.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may tie a bucket with a belt,
phrases.notes: A belt will surely be untied later, so the knot is temporary

phrases.english: but not with a rope.
Rabbi Yehuda permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹשְׁרִין דְּלִי בְּפָסִקְיָא, אֲבָל לֹא בְּחֶבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A belt is allowed and a rope is forbidden; רבי יהודה permits the rope

steps.title: רבי יהודה's rule: no liability for a temporary knot
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives a general rule: there is no liability for any knot that is not permanent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה stated a rule: Any knot that is not permanent, one is not liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי יהודה's general rule, which explains why he permits the rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מלאכה of tying (קושר) only applies fully to a permanent knot (קשר של קיימא). For רבי יהודה, a temporary knot carries no liability, so the rope tied to the bucket is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: One is not liable for it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda stated a principle:
any knot that is not permanent —
one is not liable for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי יהודה's view in Step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no liability for a non-permanent knot

steps.title: What kind of rope does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of rope the משנה is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A rope of what [kind]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about the case. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer matters because different ropes are used differently. Some stay tied for good and some are taken back later, and that decides whether the knot is permanent.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A rope of what [kind]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind the משנה in Step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of rope the משנה refers to

steps.title: A regular rope would make a permanent knot
steps.stepSummary: If the rope is an ordinary one, how could רבי יהודה permit it? Tying an ordinary rope to a bucket makes a permanent knot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say an ordinary rope, does רבי יהודה permit it? It is a permanent knot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible answer and finds a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary rope tied to a bucket usually stays there for good. That is a קשר של קיימא, and even רבי יהודה's own rule would forbid it. So the rope cannot be an ordinary one.

phrases.english: If you say an ordinary rope,
does Rabbi Yehuda permit [it]?
It is a permanent knot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as speaking about an ordinary rope
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ordinary rope makes a permanent knot, which רבי יהודה himself would forbid

steps.title: It means a weaver's rope
steps.stepSummary: The rope in the משנה is a weaver's rope (חבל דגרדי). The weaver needs it for work, so he will surely untie it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a weaver's rope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the משנה is talking about a weaver's rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A weaver needs his rope back for his work, so he will not leave it on the bucket. That makes the knot temporary, which is why רבי יהודה can permit it.

phrases.english: Rather, a weaver's rope.
phrases.notes: He needs it for his work, so he will untie it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 after Step 9 rejected the ordinary rope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rope is an ordinary rope
steps.terutzMaskana: The rope is a weaver's rope, which will surely be untied

steps.title: So the dispute is about making a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion. חכמים forbid the weaver's rope as a decree because of an ordinary rope, and רבי יהודה does not make that decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that רבנן hold we decree against a weaver's rope because of an ordinary rope, and רבי יהודה holds we do not decree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the dispute must be about. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A weaver's rope makes only a temporary knot, so חכמים must forbid it for a different reason: people might confuse it with an ordinary rope (גזירה). רבי יהודה does not make this decree. The phrasing 'is that to say' signals a problem is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces an inference that will be challenged)

phrases.english: Is that to say that the Rabbis hold

phrases.aramaic: גָּזְרִינַן חֶבֶל דְּגַרְדִּי אַטּוּ חֶבֶל דְּעָלְמָא,
phrases.english: we decree against a weaver's rope because of an ordinary rope,
and Rabbi Yehuda holds we do not decree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the answer in Step 10, setting up Step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute is really about making a גזירה, with חכמים strict and רבי יהודה lenient

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the opinions reversed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a torn bucket rope may not be knotted, but may be tied in a bow (עניבה). רבי יהודה says one may only wrap a belt around it and may not even make a bow. Here רבי יהודה is the stricter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: A bucket rope that tore, one may not knot it, but only tie it in a bow. רבי יהודה says: He wraps a belt or sash around it, as long as he does not tie it in a bow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the משנה. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, חכמים are strict and רבי יהודה is lenient. In the ברייתא, חכמים allow a bow, while רבי יהודה forbids even a bow and allows only wrapping. Each opinion seems to contradict itself, so the גמרא must explain how both sources fit.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (between two sources)
He ties it in a bow (a loose, easily undone tie)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up קושר (a real knot) and עונב (a bow). In this ברייתא, חכמים allow a bow but not a knot. רבי יהודה forbids even the bow, which is the opposite of how lenient he looked in the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The contradiction forces the גמרא to look again at what each opinion really holds. The resolution, which comes next, shapes how we understand the rules of tying on שבת.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
A bucket rope that tore —
one may not knot it, but only tie it in a bow.
And Rabbi Yehuda says:
he wraps a hollow belt or a sash around it,
provided that he does not tie it in a bow.
phrases.notes: Here רבי יהודה is stricter than חכמים

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the picture drawn in Step 11 using a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The picture that חכמים are strict and רבי יהודה is lenient about tying a bucket
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, חכמים permit a bow while רבי יהודה forbids even a bow, which reverses their positions in the משנה

steps.title: Stating the double contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem: רבי יהודה seems to contradict himself, and so do רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty between רבי יהודה and רבי יהודה, and a difficulty between רבנן and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the problem created by the ברייתא in Step 12. Both opinions seem to flip between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה is lenient about a weaver's rope and makes no decree, but in the ברייתא he forbids even a bow. רבנן are the opposite: strict in the משנה because of a decree, but in the ברייתא they allow a bow. So each side looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty; a problem that needs an answer
One statement of רבי יהודה against another statement of his; a contradiction within the same person
The Sages, the majority opinion (the same as חכמים)

phrases.english: It is difficult: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: In the משנה he is lenient; in the ברייתא he is strict.

phrases.english: and it is difficult: the Rabbis against the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: In the משנה they are strict; in the ברייתא they are lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally states the contradiction raised by the ברייתא in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The understanding from Step 11 that רבנן make a decree and רבי יהודה does not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא each side takes the opposite position from the one it takes in the משנה, so neither opinion seems consistent.

steps.title: Answering for רבנן: a rope is confused with a rope, but a bow is not confused with a knot
steps.stepSummary: רבנן make a decree only where people could really mix things up. A weaver's rope looks like any other rope, but a bow is clearly different from a knot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction in רבנן is not difficult. One rope can be confused with another rope. A bow cannot be confused with a knot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבנן are consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree is made only when there is a real chance of confusion. A weaver's rope and an ordinary rope look alike, so רבנן forbid the weaver's rope too. A bow and a knot look very different, so there is no reason to forbid the bow.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening words of an answer
Can be confused or mixed up with

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult:
a rope with a rope can be confused.
phrases.notes: A weaver's rope could be mistaken for an ordinary rope, so רבנן forbid it.

phrases.english: A bow with a knot is not confused.
phrases.notes: So there is no need to forbid the bow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: there is a risk of confusion in one case and not in the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבנן decree in one place and not in another, so they are inconsistent
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן decree only where confusion is likely. Rope with rope is likely; bow with knot is not.

steps.title: Answering for רבי יהודה: to him a bow is itself a knot
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's ban on a bow is not a decree at all. He holds that a bow counts as a real knot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction in רבי יהודה is not difficult. There, he does not forbid a bow because it could be confused with a knot. He forbids it because a bow itself is a knot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יהודה is also consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה never makes these kinds of decrees, which is why he permits the weaver's rope. He forbids the bow because, in his view, the bow is truly a knot, so it is forbidden on its own terms.

keyTerms.meaning: There; in the other source (here, the ברייתא)
Not because of this, but because of that

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה made a decree here. To him, the bow is forbidden directly because it is a knot.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides are consistent. רבנן decree only where confusion is likely (rope with rope, not bow with knot). רבי יהודה never makes these decrees, but he holds that a bow is itself a knot.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult:
there, it is not because
a bow can be confused with a knot,
rather, a bow itself is a knot.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the reason: the ban on the bow is a direct prohibition, not a decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה made a decree against the bow because it looks like a knot
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה a bow is itself a knot, so it is forbidden directly. He still makes no decrees.

steps.title: רב: one may bring a rope from home and tie it between a cow and a trough
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person may take a rope from his house and tie it to a cow and to a feeding trough on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב חייא בר אשי, in the name of רב: A person may bring a rope from inside his house and tie it to a cow and to a trough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב about tying a rope on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying the rope seems fine because it is a temporary knot; the person will surely untie it later. This ruling is about to be challenged.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
A person may bring a rope from inside his house,
and tie it to the cow and to the trough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new related ruling about tying ropes on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may bring a rope from home and tie it between a cow and a trough on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids bringing a rope from home
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא אריכא challenges רב with a ברייתא that says one may NOT bring a rope from home to tie the cow to the trough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא אריכא, who is רבי אחא בר פפא, challenged רבי אבא. A ברייתא teaches: A rope already on the trough may be tied to the cow. A rope already on the cow may be tied to the trough. But one may not bring a rope from his house and tie it to the cow and the trough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling with a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows tying only a rope that is already attached to the cow or the trough. It explicitly forbids bringing a new rope from home, which is exactly what רב allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that; only on condition that

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa Arikha raised an objection,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהוּא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר פָּפָּא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: he is Rabbi Aḥa bar Pappa, to Rabbi Abba:
A rope that is on the trough, one may tie it to the cow,
and one that is on the cow, one may tie it to the trough,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא חֶבֶל מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
phrases.english: provided that he does not bring a rope from inside his house
and tie it to the cow and to the trough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's permission to bring a rope from home
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly forbids the exact case רב permits.

steps.title: The ברייתא means an ordinary rope; רב means a weaver's rope
steps.stepSummary: The two sources talk about different ropes. The ברייתא forbids an ordinary rope, which might be left tied permanently. רב permits a weaver's rope, which will surely be untied.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is an ordinary rope. Here, it is a weaver's rope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רב and the ברייתא are discussing different kinds of rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary rope might be left on the cow and trough for good, which makes a permanent knot, so the ברייתא forbids it. A weaver needs his rope back for work, so he will untie it, and רב permits it. This matches the idea from Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Here; in this source (here, רב's ruling)

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the same distinction as Step 10: a knot that will surely be untied is not a permanent knot.

phrases.english: There, it is an ordinary rope;
phrases.notes: The ברייתא forbids it, since it may stay tied permanently.

phrases.english: here, it is a weaver's rope.
phrases.notes: רב permits it, since the weaver will untie it to use it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם חֶבֶל דְּעָלְמָא הָכָא חֶבֶל דְּגַרְדִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the type of rope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and the ברייתא disagree about the same rope
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to an ordinary rope (forbidden). רב refers to a weaver's rope (permitted).

steps.title: שמואל: weavers' tools may be moved on שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that weavers' tools may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It is permitted to move weavers' tools on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about which items may be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These tools are used for weaving, which is forbidden on שבת. Even so, שמואל permits moving them. Next, the גמרא asks how far this permission goes.

keyTerms.meaning: To move them, i.e., carry or handle them

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Weavers' tools may be moved on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic connected to weavers (after the weaver's rope)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weavers' tools may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: Asking about the upper and lower beams of the loom
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רב יהודה whether שמואל's permission includes the upper and lower beams of the loom.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב יהודה: What about the upper beam and the lower beam?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask about the limits of שמואל's ruling, and set up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beams are big, central parts of the loom, not small hand tools. So it is unclear whether the word 'tools' includes them.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him; a real question
The upper beam of the loom
The lower beam of the loom

phrases.english: They asked of Rav Yehuda:
The upper beam and the lower beam, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the scope of the ruling in Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the loom's beams count as 'weavers' tools' that may be moved

steps.title: רב יהודה is unsure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers 'yes and no.' He is not sure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes and no, and the matter was uncertain to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה cannot give a clear answer. The next step settles the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not hear from שמואל exactly how far the permission goes, so he wavers. The next step will settle the question from a different report.

keyTerms.meaning: It was loose in his hand; he was unsure

phrases.english: Yes and no, and it was uncertain in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question in Step 20 without settling it
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No clear answer; רב יהודה was uncertain

steps.title: רב נחמן's report: even the beams may be moved, but not the posts
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports שמואל's ruling more fully: weavers' tools may be moved, even the upper and lower beams, but not the posts.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: It is permitted to move weavers' tools on שבת, even the upper beam and the lower beam, but not the posts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles רב יהודה's doubt with a fuller version of שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's version includes the beams in the permission. It also adds a new limit: the posts of the loom may not be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: Posts; the standing poles of the loom

steps.whatToRemember: Weavers' tools may be moved on שבת, including the upper and lower beams, but the posts of the loom may not be moved.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Naḥman said that Shmuel said:
Weavers' tools may be moved on Shabbat,
even the upper beam and the lower beam,
but not the posts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the doubt left in Step 21
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The beams are included in the permission to move weavers' tools; the posts are excluded.

steps.title: רבא asks why the posts are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן. Why are the posts of the loom forbidden to move? Holes in the ground are not a real concern, because they form on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Why are the posts different, that they may not be moved? If you say it is because pulling them out makes holes in the ground, those holes just happen by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא questions the last part of שמואל's ruling, which forbade moving the loom's posts. He suggests a possible reason and then knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The posts were set into the ground, so pulling one out leaves a hole. רבא argues that this hole is not something the person deliberately digs. It just results by itself, so it should not be a reason to forbid moving the post.

keyTerms.meaning: posts (the upright posts of the loom, set into the ground)
holes or pits in the ground
what is different? (asking for the reason behind a distinction)

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
What is different about the posts, that they may not [be moved]?
If you say it is because he makes holes [when pulling them out],
phrases.notes: This is the suggested reason, which רבא is about to reject.

phrases.english: the holes come about on their own,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exclusion of posts in שמואל's ruling as reported by רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the loom's posts may not be moved on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only apparent reason is the holes created. But holes formed as a side effect are not forbidden, so the posts should be allowed.

steps.title: Proof from turnips buried under a vine
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה to back up his challenge. Turnips or radishes buried in the ground with some leaves showing may be pulled out on שבת, even though this leaves holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone stores turnips and radishes in the ground under a grapevine. If some of their leaves are uncovered, he need not worry about כלאים, שביעית, or מעשר. And they may be taken out on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports his point from a משנה. Pulling buried vegetables out of the ground on שבת is allowed, even though it leaves holes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person was only storing the vegetables, not planting them. So there are no planting problems (כלאים, שביעית) and no tithing problem (מעשר). The key point is the end: they may be removed on שבת. This shows the חכמים did not worry about the holes this creates.

keyTerms.meaning: one who buries or stores something (here, in the ground for safekeeping)
forbidden mixtures (here, planting food crops in a vineyard)
the Sabbatical year, when working the land is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Most of this משנה (כלאים, שביעית, מעשר) is not the point here. רבא only needs the last phrase, וניטלין בשבת. That phrase shows that making holes by pulling something out of the ground is not forbidden.

phrases.english: As we learned [in a mishnah]: One who stores turnips and radishes
under a grapevine,
if some of its leaves are uncovered,
phrases.notes: The leaves sticking out let him grab the vegetable and pull it out.

phrases.english: he need not worry, not because of mixed plantings,
and not because of the Sabbatical year,
and not because of tithes,
and they may be taken [out] on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: This is the part that proves רבא's point.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source backing רבא's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That holes formed by removing something from the ground do not make it forbidden to move on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about turnips and radishes stored under a vine (כלאים)

steps.title: A field is different from a house
steps.stepSummary: The answer: in a field, nobody bothers to fill in holes. In a house, a person will want to smooth over the holes, which is forbidden work. So the posts are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a field, a person will not come to level the holes. Here, in a house, he will come to level the holes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא. The turnip case and the loom posts are not the same, because of where the holes are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is not making the hole. The worry is that the person will then fill it in or smooth it over, which is a forbidden act on שבת. A hole in a field does not bother anyone. A hole in a house floor does, so the חכמים forbade moving the posts there.

keyTerms.meaning: to level or smooth over (filling in holes)

steps.whatToRemember: The posts are forbidden not because of the hole itself. They are forbidden out of concern that a person will fill in a hole in his house floor.

phrases.english: In a field, he will not come to level the holes,
here, in a house, he will come to level the holes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by distinguishing the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Holes form on their own, so moving the posts should be permitted, just like pulling out the turnips.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a house there is a real concern that a person will smooth over the holes, so the posts are forbidden. In a field there is no such concern.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks about the heavy loom beams
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks רבי יהודה בר ליואי whether weavers' tools like the upper and lower beams may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked רבי יהודה בר ליואי: Weavers' tools, such as the upper beam and the lower beam, may they be moved on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: A new source on the same topic begins. רבי יוחנן asks about moving the big loom beams on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the same beams that רב נחמן, quoting שמואל, said may be moved (step 22). Now a different authority is asked about them, so we may be about to see a different view.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked him (raised a question before him)
the upper beam and the lower beam of the loom
to move them (on שבת, the laws of מוקצה)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר לֵיוַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked Rabbi Yehuda bar Livai:
Weavers' tools,
such as the upper beam and the lower beam,
what is [the law] regarding moving them on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר לֵיוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the same question about the beams, now addressed to a different authority.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the upper and lower loom beams may be moved on שבת

steps.title: The beams may not be moved
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר ליואי answers that the beams may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בר ליואי gives a short answer: forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This differs from the version of שמואל's ruling in step 22, which allowed moving the beams. Here the beams are treated as forbidden to move.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 22. According to רב נחמן, שמואל allowed moving the beams. רבי יהודה בר ליואי forbids it. These are two different opinions.

phrases.english: He said to him: One may not move them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loom beams may not be moved on שבת.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks for the reason behind the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן wants to know why the beams are forbidden. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are tools, and tools can usually be moved for some purpose. So the ruling needs a special reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the answer just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the beams may not be moved

steps.title: They are never moved anyway
steps.stepSummary: The beams are forbidden because they are not normally moved even during the week. They are heavy and stay in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are not moved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בר ליואי explains that these beams are simply never moved, so they may not be moved on שבת either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beams are very heavy and stay fixed in one spot, even on weekdays. Since nobody normally moves them, they do not count as ordinary movable tools. So moving them on שבת is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: An object that is never moved even on weekdays, like a fixed heavy beam, may not be moved on שבת either.

phrases.english: Because they are not [normally] moved.
phrases.notes: They are too heavy and are treated as fixed in place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason requested.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The beams are not moved even on weekdays, so they may not be moved on שבת.

steps.title: New משנה: folding garments and making beds
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows folding garments, even several times, and making beds on Friday night for שבת day. It does not allow preparing beds on שבת for after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may fold garments, even four or five times. And one may make the beds from Friday night for שבת day, but not from שבת for after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what kinds of tidying up are allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Folding and bed-making are allowed when they are for שבת itself. Preparing on שבת for a weekday, meaning after שבת ends, is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: one may make (spread out) the beds

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that one may not prepare on שבת for after שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may fold the garments
even four or five times,
and one may make the beds
from Shabbat night for Shabbat [day],
but not from Shabbat for after Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקַפְּלִין אֶת הַכֵּלִים אֲפִילּוּ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Folding garments and making beds are allowed on שבת for שבת use, but not as preparation for after שבת.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: from יום הכיפורים to שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל allows folding and bed-making on יום הכיפורים for the שבת that follows it. He also rules that fats of שבת offerings may be burned on יום הכיפורים, but not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: One may fold garments and make beds from יום הכיפורים for שבת. And the fats of שבת offerings may be offered on יום הכיפורים, but those of יום הכיפורים may not be offered on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל adds rules for when יום הכיפורים and שבת fall back to back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יום הכיפורים falls on Friday, one may prepare on it for שבת, because that is preparing for a holier day. Likewise, leftover fats from שבת sacrifices may be burned on יום הכיפורים if it falls right after. But leftover fats from יום הכיפורים may not be burned on שבת, because שבת is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: the fats (of sacrifices, burned on the altar)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:

phrases.aramaic: מְקַפְּלִין אֶת הַכֵּלִים, וּמַצִּיעִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת
phrases.english: One may fold the garments and make the beds
from Yom Kippur for Shabbat.
phrases.notes: When יום הכיפורים falls on Friday.

phrases.english: And the fats of Shabbat [offerings] are offered on Yom Kippur,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: but not those of Yom Kippur on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: שבת is stricter than יום הכיפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further opinion within the משנה about the relationship between יום הכיפורים and שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום הכיפורים one may fold garments and make beds for the שבת that follows. Fats of שבת offerings may be burned on יום הכיפורים, but fats of יום הכיפורים offerings may not be burned on שבת, because שבת is the stricter day.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: neither direction
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees about the fats. Neither may שבת fats be burned on יום הכיפורים, nor may יום הכיפורים fats be burned on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: The fats of שבת are not offered on יום הכיפורים, and the fats of יום הכיפורים are not offered on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the opposing view on the fats. It works both ways: neither day's fats may be burned on the other day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל treated שבת as stricter, so he allowed one direction. רבי עקיבא treats the two days as equal on this matter, so he forbids both directions.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל sees שבת as stricter than יום הכיפורים, so he allows one direction. רבי עקיבא forbids both directions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שֶׁל שַׁבָּת קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: Neither are those of Shabbat offered on Yom Kippur,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים קְרֵיבִין בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: nor are those of Yom Kippur offered on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי ישמעאל's ruling about the fats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fats may not be burned from שבת on יום הכיפורים or from יום הכיפורים on שבת.

steps.title: Folding is allowed only by one person
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי limits the permission to fold. It applies only when one person folds alone, not when two people fold together.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The school of רבי ינאי said: The משנה only taught this when one person folds. But when two people fold together, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins narrowing the משנה's permission to fold garments. This first limit is about how many people are folding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people folding together make the garment much neater and flatter, almost like pressing or repairing it. That is too close to fixing the garment, so it is forbidden. One person folding alone is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: they only taught this in the case of (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The school of Rabbi Yanai said:
They only taught this regarding one person,
but regarding two people, no.
phrases.notes: Two people folding together is like repairing the garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins limiting the משנה's permission to fold garments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Folding on שבת is permitted only when one person does it alone.

steps.title: Only new garments
steps.stepSummary: Even one person may fold only new garments, not old ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even with one person, we only said this for new garments, but not old ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit: the garment must be new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new garment looks fine whether or not it is folded, so folding it is not a real fix. An old garment truly gets fixed up by folding, so folding it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this when (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: And even with one person,
we only said this regarding new [garments],
but regarding old ones, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְאָדָם אֶחָד נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בַּחֲדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limiting condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Folding is permitted only for new garments.

steps.title: Only white garments
steps.stepSummary: Even new garments may be folded only if they are white, not colored.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even with new garments, we only said this for white ones, but not colored ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third limit: the garment must be white.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condition is stacked on top of the one before it. The permission keeps getting narrower and narrower.

phrases.english: And even with new ones, we only said this
regarding white ones,
but regarding colored ones, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וָחֳדָשִׁים נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בִּלְבָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third limiting condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Folding is permitted only for white garments.

steps.title: Only if he has nothing else to wear
steps.stepSummary: The final limit: folding is allowed only if the person has no other garment to change into for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said this when he has nothing else to change into. But if he has something else to change into, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the fourth and last limit. This completes the narrowing of the משנה's permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he has other clothes to wear, folding this garment is not needed for שבת. It would really be for a later day, so it is forbidden. Only when he needs this exact garment again on שבת may he fold it.
steps.whatToRemember: Folding on שבת is allowed only if all four conditions are met: one person, a new garment, a white garment, and no other garment to change into.

phrases.english: And we only said this
when he has nothing to change into,
but if he has something to change into, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לְהַחֲלִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the fourth and final limiting condition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's permission to fold garments applies only to one person folding a new, white garment when he has nothing else to wear.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's household did not fold their white clothes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבן גמליאל's household did not fold their white garments on שבת, because they had other garments to change into.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The people of רבן גמליאל's household did not fold their white clothes, because they had other clothes to change into.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the last rule. Folding is only allowed for someone who has nothing else to wear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 36 said folding is allowed only if a person has no other garment for שבת. רבן גמליאל's household owned white clothes, the very kind that may be folded. Still, they did not fold them, because they had spare clothes. This shows the 'no change of clothes' condition was a real limit that people followed in practice.

phrases.english: It was taught: Those of the household of Rabban Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ מְקַפְּלִים כְּלֵי לָבָן שֶׁלָּהֶן,
phrases.english: would not fold their white garments,
because they had others to change into.
phrases.notes: Being wealthy, they had spare garments, so the permission to fold did not apply to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the final limit in step 36 (folding only if one has no other garment) with a real-life case.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that folding is allowed only when one has no other garment to change into.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing the practice of רבן גמליאל's household.
steps.whatToRemember: Folding clothes on שבת is allowed only under all the limits together: one person, new clothes, white clothes, and no other clothes to change into. רבן גמליאל's household had spare clothes, so they did not fold.

steps.title: רב הונא: change clothes, or let your clothes hang loose
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches how to honor שבת through clothing. If you have other clothes, change into them. If not, let your garments hang down loosely as a sign of honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If he has clothes to change into, he should change. If he has nothing to change into, he should let his clothes hang down long.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives practical advice for honoring שבת through how you dress. He covers both someone who has extra clothes and someone who does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic idea is that a person should look different on שבת. Someone with a second set of clothes should simply wear it. Someone without one can still change how he wears his only clothes. In those days wealthy people wore their garments loose and hanging down, so wearing them that way showed honor for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He should let his garments hang down loosely

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
If he has clothes to change into — he should change,
and if he does not have clothes to change into —
he should let his garments hang down.
phrases.notes: Wearing clothes long and loose was the style of the wealthy, so it shows special respect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ לְהַחֲלִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of folding to a related one: how to show honor for שבת through clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Change into other clothes if you can. If you cannot, let your garments hang down loosely in honor of שבת.

steps.title: רב ספרא: doesn't this look like arrogance?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא objects that letting one's garments hang down like the wealthy looks like haughtiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא challenged this: But doesn't that look like arrogance?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא attacks רב הונא's advice. Dressing like a rich person might look like showing off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is how it looks to others. Wearing garments long and loose was a sign of wealth and status. An ordinary person who suddenly dresses that way may seem to be putting on airs, which is the opposite of what we want.

phrases.english: Rav Safra strongly objected to it:
But doesn't it look like haughtiness?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב סָפְרָא: וְהָא מִיתְחֲזֵי כְּרָמוּת רוּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's advice in step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's advice to let one's garments hang down.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dressing in the style of the wealthy looks like arrogance, which is improper.

steps.title: It is clearly for שבת, so it is not arrogance
steps.stepSummary: Since he does not dress this way every day and does it only now, people see it is in honor of שבת, not arrogance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he does not do this every day, and he is doing it only now, it does not look like arrogance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב ספרא. Because the person only dresses this way on שבת, everyone understands why he is doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arrogance would be someone dressing like a rich person all the time to show off. Here the change happens only on שבת, so onlookers connect it to שבת. The context changes what the act means, and רב הונא's advice stands.

phrases.english: Since every day he does not do so,
and it is only now that he does so —
it does not look like haughtiness.
phrases.notes: People can tell he is doing it for שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ספרא's challenge in step 39 and defends רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Context reframes the act: a once-a-week change is understood as honoring שבת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dressing like the wealthy always looks like arrogance.
steps.terutzMaskana: When done only on שבת, it clearly shows honor for שבת and is not arrogance.
steps.whatToRemember: Honoring שבת through dress is encouraged. Even a person with only one set of clothes can wear it differently, and it is not arrogance because it is plainly for שבת.

steps.title: 'And you shall honor it': שבת clothes should differ from weekday clothes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'וְכִבַּדְתּוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת דְּרָכֶיךָ' and learns from 'וְכִבַּדְתּוֹ' that one's שבת clothing should not be like weekday clothing. רבי יוחנן called his clothes 'my honorers'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And you shall honor it by not doing your ways.' From 'And you shall honor it' we learn that your שבת clothing should not be like your weekday clothing. This is like רבי יוחנן, who called his clothes 'my honorers'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section explaining a פסוק in ישעיה phrase by phrase. The first lesson is about special clothing for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a source in the פסוק for the clothing theme just discussed. To 'honor' שבת includes looking different, so special clothes are part of כבוד שבת. רבי יוחנן's name for his clothes, 'my honorers', shows that clothing gives a person dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall honor it (from ישעיה 58:13)
My honorers (רבי יוחנן's name for his clothes)

phrases.english: "And you shall honor it by not doing your ways" (Isaiah 58:13).
phrases.notes: This quotes the פסוק that the following lines explain.

phrases.english: "And you shall honor it" — that your Shabbat clothing should not be
like your weekday clothing,
and like that of Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who would call his clothes "my honorers."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the theme of honoring שבת through clothing and opens a phrase-by-phrase reading of the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Your שבת clothing should be different from your weekday clothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the widespread practice of wearing special clothes on שבת.

steps.title: 'Not doing your ways': שבת walking should differ from weekday walking
steps.stepSummary: From 'מֵעֲשׂוֹת דְּרָכֶיךָ' the גמרא learns that a person's way of walking on שבת should not be like his weekday walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Not doing your ways' means that your walking on שבת should not be like your walking on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the פסוק. Even the way you walk should change on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first lesson was about how you look. This one is about how you move. 'Your ways' is read literally as your walking. On weekdays people hurry around for their business, and on שבת one should walk in a calmer, more restful way.

phrases.english: "Not doing your ways" —
that your walking on Shabbat should not be
like your walking on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מֵעֲשׂוֹת דְּרָכֶיךָ״ — שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הִילּוּכְךָ שֶׁל שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק with its next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Your way of walking on שבת must differ from your weekday walking.

steps.title: 'From pursuing your affairs': your business is forbidden, Heaven's affairs are permitted
steps.stepSummary: From 'מִמְּצוֹא חֶפְצְךָ' the גמרא learns that personal weekday affairs are forbidden on שבת, but matters of Heaven (מצוה-related matters) are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From pursuing your affairs' means: your own affairs are forbidden, but the affairs of Heaven are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains another phrase of the פסוק. It draws a line between your own business and מצוה business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'your' in 'your affairs' is the key. The פסוק only forbids personal, weekday matters on שבת. Matters of Heaven, meaning things connected to מצוות and community needs, are not 'yours', so they are allowed.

phrases.english: "From pursuing your affairs" —
your affairs are forbidden,
affairs of Heaven are permitted.
phrases.notes: For example, things connected to מצוות or community needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק with its next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Personal weekday matters are forbidden on שבת. Matters of Heaven are permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about forbidden מלאכה. It is about what you deal with and talk about on שבת. Even things that are not מלאכה can be improper if they are weekday business, and מצוה matters are allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for allowing discussion and arrangement of מצוה and communal needs on שבת.

steps.title: 'And speaking a word': setting up the next explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the פסוק, 'וְדַבֵּר דָּבָר', and its explanation continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And speaking a word' —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by quoting the next phrase of the פסוק. The explanation comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only quotes the words to be explained. The lesson about how speech on שבת should differ from weekday speech follows next. Do not look for a ruling here yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And speaking a word / idle talk

phrases.english: "And speaking a word" —
phrases.notes: Its explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the phrase-by-phrase reading of the פסוק and introduces the last phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: introduces the phrase about speech on שבת, which is explained next.
